correctness.rationale: The monomial power S_beta^m z^j=beta^{mj+m(m-1)/2} z^{j+m} gives the exact norm factor beta^{m(m-1)/2}. Positive-real normalized Szegő-kernel overlap forces conjugate(a)b real; swapping ordered kernels excludes the larger-input branch and reduces to F_m(s)=q s^m(1-s²)/[1-(1-alpha)ks-alpha s²], alpha=beta^m, k=sqrt(1-q²). Differentiating yields the stated quartic P_m. Its derivative is convex and has nonpositive endpoint values, implying unique interior zero u_m; P_m(h)>0 for h=k/(1+q) makes that zero admissible. The sign of P_m(k) produces the opposite/origin/aligned transition q²=(1-alpha)/(m+1-alpha), strictly decreasing in m. Uniform convergence of denominators and the stationary logarithmic derivative show u_m→1 and m(1-u_m)→1, hence the universal normalized limit 2q/[e(1-k)]. Rotation and a continuous radial path establish the CLOSED disk, not just the circle. Independent symbolic derivative identities and ~100 bounded stationary-point/kernel checks support algebra only, not the unbounded m limit.
